# Neat Racing Voxel Racer (neatRacing)

**Status:** [WIP]

<!-- Derived from plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md (spec sections 13, 17, 18, 12.4-12.5).
     This is the tracker for the neatRacing voxel racer flagship demo. Phase/step/slice
     structure mirrors spec section 17 phases P1/P2/P3 1:1 with slice_ids kept verbatim
     so section 18 traceability holds without renumbering. Planning-only authoring pass:
     no src/, docs/, examples/, or scripts/ production edits. -->

## Scope

- Implement the neatRacing voxel racer per `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md`:
  Phase 1 graphics engine + manual keyboard driving (AC-001..AC-024 + AC-040..AC-042),
  Phase 2 AI migration with NGE growth engine (AC-025..AC-034 + AC-043),
  Phase 3 polish + deprecation prep (AC-035..AC-039).
- Planning-only pass in this instance: author full machine-readable step packets,
  register the plan, rebind the session, reindex RAG, prove gates. Execution is
  dispatched step-by-step to implementing/testing specialists after verification.
- Single source of truth for acceptance criteria and validation commands is the spec
  (section 13 ACs, section 12.5 conventions); this tracker binds each spec slice to its
  ACs, files, red-test notes, and validation commands.

## Mandates

- **Planning-only:** this authoring pass edits only `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`,
  `plans/README.md`, `plans/Roadmap.md`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, and RAG index artifacts.
- **Spec lock:** spec section 12 locked decisions register (LD) and resolved open
  questions are not reopened by the tracker. Deprecation prep is notices-only
  (LD-33); removal of `examples/racing_curriculum` is a separate user-confirmed
  workstream and out of scope.
- **Machine-readable packets:** every execution step carries a YAML packet with
  `expansion: slices`, `auto_expand: true`, `tdd_sequence: green-only`, and typed
  slices (slice_id / title / status / goal / estimate_hours / files_to_change /
  acceptance_criteria / parallelizable / dependencies) per the step-packet gate schema.
- **Slice discipline:** each slice is one atomic behavioral intent bound to spec
  section 17; at most 3 code files per slice (sibling `*.test.ts` files count;
  trivial one-line config registrations such as a package.json script line or a
  tsconfig include may accompany without counting); estimate_hours <= 4.
- **Red-first:** every implementation slice carries `red_test` notes (the failing
  assertion to author first) honoring the spec RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN rule; each
  step ends with a green-testing slice that runs the section 12.5 validation list.
- **Named constants:** tuning values use the named constants from the spec open
  questions patch (NEATRACING_FIXED_RENDER_HEIGHT, NEATRACING_MAX_BACKING_WIDTH,
  NEATRACING_AI_MIN_SESSION_LAPS, NEATRACING_EDITOR_UNDO_BUDGET_BYTES,
  NEATRACING_REBUILD_P95_BUDGET_MS, NEATRACING_ADAPTATION_TICK_BUDGET_MS, etc.).
- **Zero per-frame allocation (P9)** and **capacity limits preserved** (maxNodes 8000 /
  maxConnections 32000, AC-029) are standing constraints on all Phase 1/2 slices.
- **No deferred cleanup:** when a slice replaces an existing module or script, the old
  code is removed in the same slice.
- **No git:** agents never run git commands; all changes land via direct file edits.
- **Evidence:** gate runs are recorded in `## Latest validation evidence`; green-light
  recording is reserved for the separate verification instance.

### Derivation notes

1. **1:1 slice preservation:** spec section 17 slice_ids (P1-S1-A .. P3-S2-C) appear
   verbatim with their spec file lists and AC bindings; section 18 traceability holds
   without renumbering. The tracker adds one trailing green-testing slice per execution
   step (id `<spec-step>-green`, e.g. `P1-S1-green`) to host the section 12.5
   validation sweep; spec impl slices keep goal `implementing`.
2. **a/b step splits:** spec steps with 5 impl slices (P1-S3, P1-S4, P1-S6, P1-S7,
   P2-S3) are split into part 1 (A-C) and part 2 (D-E) sub-steps because a
   gate-conformant green-only step needs at least 2 and at most 5 slices and a
   trailing green-testing slice (5 impl + 1 green = 6 > 5). Spec slice_ids, file
   lists, and AC bindings are unchanged by the split.
3. **Uniform green-only tdd_sequence:** spec slices are RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN
   atomic units; per-slice RED notes live in the slice `red_test` field so the
   gate-conformant step shape is uniformly `green-only` (all-but-last slices
   `implementing`, last slice `green-testing`).
4. **Planning ACs** use the AC-PLN-001..AC-PLN-005 prefix to avoid collision with the
   spec AC-001..AC-043 numbering.
5. **Dual-parser layout contract:** two parsers coexist and this tracker satisfies both.
   The step-packet GATE parses only the fenced YAML packets (heading-agnostic). The
   neataptic-workflow MCP additionally parses HEADINGS scoped to `## Implementation
phases`: `### Phase <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H3 + em-dash, terminated by a
   `## …validation gates…` H2) and `#### Step <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H4) inside the
   phase body; the active [WIP] step also carries `**Step objective:**` and
   `**Required validation:**` prose sections (backtick commands prefix-matching the
   YAML `validation` list). Keep this shape on every future step flip.
6. **Global step numbering:** the coverage backlog `Step` column uses global
   step numbers across phases — Phase 1 = 02-15 (Step 13 = P1-boot-glue
   wiring; Step 14 = browser composition, inserted between Step 13 and the
   exit check per the batch-102 integration-gap classification; Step 15 =
   editor editing-loop composition, inserted between Step 14 and the exit
   check per the batch-105 editing-loop scope correction, patch #2),
   Phase 2 = 16-20, Phase 3 = 21-22. Phase 2/3 rows were renumbered from
   the pre-insertion global sequence (batch 19 item 78 obs a), re-renumbered
   after the batch-102 Step 14 insertion, and re-renumbered again after the
   batch-105 Step 15 insertion (the batch-26 renumber precedent) so
   "13"/"14"/"15" bind uniquely to Phase 1 steps and Phase 2 starts at
   global 16.

**User instruction:** Implement USER-CLAR-9 from user-bug-report-2026-10-16-14D (2026-10-20 notes): seated spectator sprites must face TOWARD the car (camera-relative atlas frame index), there must be exactly ONE sprite row per bleacher LEVEL with every level populated, ONLY ONE bleacher may host sprites with no mechanics or other people anywhere in the right world (supersedes the USER-CLAR-4 inner-ring mechanics placement clause), and the open P1-bleacher-crowd OBS-D must be reconciled with a test (atlas width/height bounded by gl.MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE read from gl.getParameter, over-limit throw path covered).

**Step objective:** Rebuild the right-world crowd so the visible result matches USER-CLAR-9: spectators face the car, exactly one sprite row sits on each of the 3 bleacher levels, exactly one bleacher is populated, the mechanic/crew people path is gone, and the sprite atlas stays within the GPU texture limit. Retires the four-slice USER-CLAR-5/6 packet (P1-bleacher-shape / P1-sprite-spacing / P1-world-lighting-coherence / P1-right-world-clar-green); their green AC-065/AC-066/AC-067 remain in force and are re-asserted by the green slice. PATCH (2026-10-20, fix iteration 3): the AC-069/AC-070 contracts were sharpened after an independent verification instance proved three contract defects (B1 anchor order, B2 personal-space knife-edge, B3 vacuous/non-seed-invariant RED-C). The three sharpenings are: (i) the narrowed seat anchors are returned in LEVEL-INTERLEAVED (round-robin) order so a sequential consumer under a finite pick budget still populates all 3 levels; (ii) the 1 m personal space is enforced through the NAMED margin constant NEATRACING_ROBOT_PERSONAL_SPACE_EPSILON_M with the effective 1 m clearance unchanged; (iii) the single host is chosen by the NAMED rule (largest getBleacherHostingFootprintArea, ties broken by the lowest prop index) and the RED-C assertions are the three real, seed-invariant ones (no people props, public-only 144-frame atlas, one hosting bleacher per fixture seed).

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the four USER-CLAR-9 contracts have failing RED contracts that then pass, the mechanic/crew/team-banner path is deleted with no leftover references, the atlas bound is read from the GL device and the over-limit throw path is tested, jest (track|engine) and neatRacing tsc are clean, the build passes, the visible-window smoke confirms the four USER-CLAR-9 items, and the coverage backlog rows AC-068..AC-071 are recorded.
- **Blocked:** a facing, anchor, hosting, or atlas seam cannot be closed inside files_to_change — record the blocker and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper.

Step 14E stays the last audited step and its audit scope now includes 14K; Step 15 keeps 14K as a prerequisite.

**User instruction:** "crowd sprites look giant-sized; reduce sprite height to 1/2 current on right-world crowd billboards" (SPRITE-1). The report is the anchor user-bug-report-2026-10-23-sprite-scale at the end of this plan, raised during the same live-page review that PASSED the Step 14K user visual gate ("looking great").

**Step objective:** Halve the world size of the right-world crowd billboards so the spectators stop reading as giant-sized next to the car. The rendered world HEIGHT of every crowd billboard - the seated spectators, the team-colored inner-ring mechanics, the slow walkers and the standing off-bleacher spectators - becomes EXACTLY 1/2 of its pre-14L height, with the world WIDTH following the SAME factor so the square 192x192 px atlas frames keep their aspect ratio. The factor is ONE named exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5 in examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts, applied inside computeBillboardScale so the placement footprint and the rendered quad can never disagree; the meters-per-sprite-pixel constant stays 0.05 m/px, so a 192 px frame goes from 9.6 m tall to 4.8 m. The halving changes the GEOMETRY only: the crowd counts, the per-frame billboard budget, the camera-relative facing, the 1 m personal space and the atlas bound all stay exactly as they are (AC-077).

**Decision set (2026-10-23 planning amendment):**

- **D1 - placement:** Step 14L is inserted between Step 14K and Step 14G, so the document order equals the routing-chain order 14F -> 14J -> 14K -> 14L -> 14G -> 14H -> 14I -> 14E -> Step 15. The anchor asks for the step "inserted before Step 14E" and "ahead of Step 14G"; the 14K precedent (D1 of the 14K decision set) is followed - the new step is placed at the HEAD of the still-open chain, immediately before 14G, so the 14L/14G demotion-and-requeue pair is one adjacent swap. Step 14E stays the last audited step and its audit scope now includes 14L; Step 15 keeps 14L as a prerequisite.
- **D2 - the single active boundary:** Phase 1 may hold only ONE [WIP] step (mcp-plan-utils.mjs loadActivePlanContext). The anchor makes 14L the new active boundary, so 14L is opened as [WIP] and Step 14G is DEMOTED to [PLANNED] (the 14K demotion pattern). No 14G work is lost: all its slices are DONE automated-green and only the user drift-feel / body-yaw visual verdict plus fix-packet-P1-turn-drift-green-iteration-11 stay open, re-queued after 14L.
- **D3 - uniform factor, not a height-only factor:** the anchor says "reduce sprite HEIGHT to 1/2 current". A height-only factor would SQUASH the square 192x192 px atlas frames, so the world WIDTH follows the SAME 0.5 factor and the rendered HEIGHT is still exactly 1/2 of the previous height - the literal request is satisfied without distorting the art. The alternative (a width-only factor) would leave the height unchanged and would NOT satisfy the request. This is recorded as a non-blocking note for the user; the sprite ATLAS is not re-drawn and no new frames are authored.
- **D4 - one named lever, applied at the single choke point:** the factor lives in ONE exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5, and it is applied INSIDE computeBillboardScale (public.sprite.ts:705). That function is the only scale source for BOTH the placement footprint (billboardWorldHalfSize, public.sprite.ts:1843) and the rendered quad (buildBillboardUpload, right-world.pass.ts:887), so the two can never disagree. The module-private BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 1.0 is removed in the same slice, and the off-bleacher footprint probe at public.sprite.ts:1486-1489 is re-authored onto the named constant, because it currently reads the raw private constant and would otherwise diverge from the rendered size.
- **D5 - the duplicated meters-per-pixel twin is removed:** right-world.pass.ts:107 keeps a byte-for-byte copy of the public.sprite.ts meters-per-pixel constant (0.05). The constant is EXPORTED from public.sprite.ts and IMPORTED by the pass, and the local copy is deleted in the same slice (no deferred cleanup). Leaving two copies alive while introducing a third factor would create exactly the drift the step is meant to remove.
- **D6 - the AC-054 absolute clause is superseded, the RATIO clause is retained:** AC-054 required a billboard to render at the same world size as a same-world-size voxel. A uniform 0.5 factor breaks that absolute clause by design, while the perspective-parity RATIO clause (a distant sprite keeps the same relative size, because the shared focal/distance projection is untouched) stays green. The stale 1:1 assertions in public.sprite.test.ts are RE-AUTHORED in the slice that changes the constant, not deferred: the 1:1 test becomes a 1:2 test against the named constant, and the absolute same-world-size test becomes a named-constant-relative 1/2 assertion.
- **D7 - the personal space is NOT sprite-derived:** the 1 m personal space (NEATRACING_ROBOT_PERSONAL_SPACE_M in right-world.builder.ts) and the off-bleacher clearance (NEATRACING_PUBLIC_OFF_BLEACHER_PERSONAL_SPACE_CLEARANCE_M = 1 m - epsilon in public.sprite.ts) are FIXED constants. The halving makes the personal-space band MORE permissive (the sprites occupy less world area), which can only INCREASE the admitted crowd, never starve it - and the anchoring-capacity filter that governs the seated population is size-independent, so the 12-per-bleacher and 240-total counts are expected to stay exact. A RED guard asserts both, because a count drift must never be silently accepted.
- **D8 - distance independence is preserved:** computeBillboardScale keeps ignoring its distance argument. The perspective shrink of a distant crowd sprite stays the shared focal/distance projection, so the halving is a pure world-size change and not a second, competing per-distance scale (a per-distance factor would have broken the AC-054 RATIO contract and the projection parity with same-world-size voxels).
- **D9 - slice discipline:** four sequential slices, each within the <= 3 files and <= 4 h budget, strictly ordered because the slice files overlap: P1-sprite-scale-red-contracts (red-testing) -> P1-sprite-scale-world-factor (implementing, public.sprite.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-render-quad (implementing, right-world.pass.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-green (green-testing, trackers). The two implementation slices are SEPARATE so that the placement footprint and the rendered quad are never half-migrated by a single oversized edit, and each implementation slice owns the test file it changes.
- **D10 - green-light ownership:** this authoring instance does NOT grant the green light. A fresh 01-planning verification instance records the green light in the Latest validation evidence section before Step 14L enters execution; the authoring instance must not self-dispatch a patch cycle.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** all four slices green; AC-077 proven by the focused suites and by the rendered-quad measurement; the AC-054 RATIO contract and the retained invariants re-asserted green; the visible-window smoke shows the crowd sprites at roughly human scale next to the car, still standing on the bleacher level, with the same counts and no atlas upload error; the coverage backlog, AC-PLN-003, README/Roadmap, and the handoff query updated.
- **Blocked:** a slice cannot meet its file or estimate budget, the halved footprint seats a spectator BELOW the bleacher surface or drops one to the ground, a crowd count drifts at any fixture seed, or the halving cannot be proven on the rendered quad - record the blocker in the Latest validation evidence section and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper. Never lower the 1/2 factor, the 12-per-bleacher count, or the 1 m personal space silently, and never let the sprite size drive the personal space.

**Required validation:**

- `npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine"`
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit`
- manual: `npm run build:neatRacing` + visible-window browser smoke on the served `/` page (the crowd sprites are visibly HALF their previous size, a seated spectator is about 4.8 m tall instead of 9.6 m and reads at roughly human scale next to the 1.2 m car, the seated spectators still stand ON the bleacher level, the seated count per bleacher is still 12, the off-bleacher walkers, standing spectators and team-colored mechanics are still present, the seated spectators still face TOWARD the car, and there is no WebGL atlas upload error)

## Validation gates

Step-level `validation` lists inside each packet are the authoritative per-step command
sources (MCP allowlist authority: `active-step.validation`). Consolidated gate routing:

- `slice-advancement` — consolidates plan-sync + step-packet + plan-slice-quality +
  plan-command-lint + shared-validation + code-coverage + specialist-review; run per
  active slice/step handoff. The Step 01 authoring pass is captured in
  `## Latest validation evidence`.
- `cortex-index` — RAG freshness + workflow/ corpus MCP liveness; rerun after every
  tracker edit batch (see `rag-index/reindex-plan-family.mjs` + `build-index` +
  `validate-index` recovery loop).
- `agent-graph` — only after any agent delegation change. `learning-event` — only after
  discovering a workflow gap or improvement.

## Deferred questions

None. The spec records all open questions RESOLVED (section 20); the tracker introduces
no new NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers. If execution uncovers a spec conflict, stop and
escalate via `00.cross-tier-helper` before deviating.

- **OPEN (2026-10-24, Step 14N) — the drift-feel DIRECTION.** The 2026-10-24 user drift
  verdict accepted the drift MECHANICS and asked for the drift FEEL to be sharpened, but it
  did NOT name the direction: a BIGGER, more visible SLIDE and a CRISPER, faster RECOVERY
  are two different products and are not interchangeable (a crisper recovery SHORTENS the
  slide, a bigger slide LENGTHENS it). The direction is therefore NOT decided in the plan
  and NOT invented by the Step 14G green closure: it is an EXPLICIT decision of the RED
  slice `P1-drift-feel-red`, which measures the current baseline (the drift proxy
  0.049388550574608114 rad over 81 frames in the 2026-10-24 final run), pins the chosen
  direction with a NAMED lever, records that decision in this plan BEFORE any production
  edit, and asks the USER to confirm the choice before the implementing slice runs. If the
  user names a direction before the RED slice starts, the recorded decision is the user's
  and the RED slice pins it verbatim.

Measured on the real pipeline (8 fixture seeds, seated billboards only): level-major → `levelsTouched = 2` at EVERY seed, per-level `[4,2,0] / [4,4,0] / [5,2,0] / [5,5,0] / [5,5,0] / [5,4,0] / [5,3,0]`, level index 2 receiving ZERO sprites; level-interleaved → `levelsTouched = 3` at EVERY seed, per-level `[2,2,2] / [3,2,2] / [3,3,2] / [3,2,2] / [4,4,4] / [4,4,3] / [3,3,3] / [3,3,3]`. Measured shortfall envelope (8 fixture seeds x EVERY bleacher x the front row of EVERY level): the nominal 1 m spacing computes to `0.99999999999997014` .. `1.0000000000000195` — a worst-case shortfall of **2.99e-14 m** and a worst-case overshoot of **1.95e-14 m** — and at seed 4242 bleacher[2] ALL SIX gaps of a level fall below 1.0. ```yaml
fix_packet:
  id: fix-packet-P1-turn-drift-green-iteration-10
  slice_id: P1-turn-drift-green
  source: 'user visual report — sixth check 2026-10-12 ~17:3x-04:00 (OBS-23 hex boundary z-fight, OBS-24 tire shadow missing; body shadow RESOLVED by user)'
  status: OBSERVATIONS
  goal: address-requested-changes
  root_cause_analysis_OBS_23: |
    Three nearly-coplanar paint layers fight in depth at gameplay angles: matte slab top face,
    hex fill at PAINT_Y=0.02 expanded outward +0.02 (HEX_FILL_OVERLAP_M), bright stroke at
    PAINT_Y+0.003 spanning apothem±0.116 across each shared boundary. At shallow angles/far
    distance the subpixel depth differences interleave, so near-black slab fragments bleed
    through along every interior tile boundary => the 'black outline or gap' the user reports.
    The iteration-9 hairline strategy (overlap + second y layer) IS the double-coverage that
    produces the seam.
  expected_changes_OBS_23:
    - 'examples/neatRacing/track/road-edge.ts — REMOVE the two-layer scheme: emit fill polygons that abut the stroke inner boundary EXACTLY (shared-vertex/t-junction-free geometry on ONE paint plane), stroke on the shared boundary edge, one y offset for ALL road-edge paint above the slab; delete HEX_FILL_OVERLAP_M and NEATRACING_ROAD_EDGE_STROKE_Y_OFFSET_M or make all paint share a single y; no coplanar double coverage anywhere.'
    - 'examples/neatRacing/track/road-edge.test.ts — assert single-plane paint: every road-edge vertex has one y value; fill outer vertices coincide with stroke inner vertices (no overlap, no gap geometry); adjacent tiles share edge geometry with no duplicate dark fill between strokes.'
    - 'docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html — replace the hairline/threshold check with a boundary-pixel assertion robust to distance: no near-black fragment clusters along interior tile boundaries at two camera distances (near + far), per user-visible contract.'
    - 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md — amend AC-046 §6.8 layering: single paint plane, shared-vertex abutment, no layered y deltas.'
  expected_changes_OBS_24:
    - 'examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/car.pass.ts — extend shadow coverage to the tire contact patches (per-wheel contact dark quads at the same paint y as the body blob, alpha matched, or reshape the blob footprint to include wheels); body-only quad is insufficient (user: body shadow OK, tires need shadow).'
    - 'examples/neatRacing/engine/lighting.test.ts — assert per-wheel contact patch positions under each wheel world position and coverage >= tire footprint.'
  user_quotes:
    - 'body now has shadow, but tires still need shadow'
    - 'the gap in the floor is still there, I would have expected this was an esy fix! what is the black outline or probably a gap on the hexagons, it should be easy to find'
  constraints:
    - 'PRESERVE: single 5 m floor grid; honeycomb 2 m hexes; shared edges emitted once; border order green 0-2m/yellow 2-4m/red 4-6m outward (user-confirmed); bright stroke IS the outline; body blob shadow (works per user); tire world-space fixed-light shading (uSunDirection dot world).'
    - 'Single paint plane for ALL road-edge hex paint is the acceptance bar: any pixel on an interior tile boundary at near or far gameplay camera must be fill or stroke color, never slab/slab-dark.'
    - 'Shadow quad must remain depth-write-off and below wheels visually; do not shade tires darker via albedo (that is OBS-20, keep light-space behavior).'
    - 'Fixture harness CDP hang is a known environment blocker: validation of the boundary-pixel contract may use a real-page screenshot probe instead of the synthetic fixture when the fixture cannot be driven; record which was used.'
    - 'Keep bundle rebuild + preflight (targeted jest road-edge/lighting, tsc, build:neatRacing, eslint changed files).'
  stop_conditions:
    - 'Do NOT change Step 14D/14E scope or advance planned steps.'
    - 'Do NOT reintroduce per-layer y offsets between fill and stroke.'
    - 'Do NOT change drift/at-speed physics (OBS-22 -> planning).'
  suggested_next_agent: 'webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer, then fresh 05-green-testing'
  estimate_hours: 3

## PlanUpdate - fix-packet-P1-crowd-facing-relative-iteration-1

```yaml
plan_update:
  slice_id: 'P1-crowd-facing-relative'
  fix_packet_id: 'fix-packet-P1-crowd-facing-relative-iteration-1'
  step: 'Step 14J'
  status: REOPENED
  role: '04-implementing'
  iteration: 1
  reviewer: 'webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer (dispatched by review-coordinator)'
  verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES
  blocking_findings:
    - id: 'F1'
      file: 'examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts'
      location: 'resolveCameraRelativeDirectionIndex - the relativeYaw line'
      finding: 'The conversion transplants the Neatenstein CCW-compass algebra (relativeYaw = cameraYaw + PI - facingYaw) onto the neatRacing compass (yaw = atan2(dx, dz), 0 rad = +Z). The lateral sense is therefore MIRRORED: a spectator whose nose points to the camera SCREEN-RIGHT resolves to index 6 (left) instead of index 2 (right). Front and back are unaffected, so the RED-A assertions alone could not detect it.'
      evidence:
        - 'browser-entry.ts lookAtInto sets the view xAxis to (-fZ, 0, fX): the camera right axis is the forward axis rotated -90 deg in the neatRacing compass, so a robot facing screen-right has facingYaw = cameraYaw - 90 deg.'
        - 'right-world.pass.ts uploads the atlas rows verbatim (no U flip) and the billboard quad maps u1 (image-right) onto +cameraRight, so image-right equals screen-right.'
        - 'examples/neatenstein/robot-sprite-data.js: the right frame (line 429) puts the visor on the IMAGE-right side of the head and the left frame (line 1237) is its exact mirror, so index 2 means nose toward screen-right.'
      required_change: 'relativeYaw = facingYaw - cameraYaw + Math.PI, which yields 0 = front (faces the camera), 2 = right (screen-right), 4 = back, 6 = left (screen-left). Correct the helper JSDoc: state the neatRacing-compass form, the art anchor, and that the Neatenstein algebra is mirrored because Neatenstein uses the opposite (CCW) compass handedness.'
    - id: 'F2'
      file: 'examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.test.ts'
      location: 'expectedCameraRelativeDirection (lines 191-208) plus its doc block (lines 171-190); the EXPECTED NEW API doc block (lines 210-235)'
      finding: 'The RED expectation helper re-implements the implementation algebra, so it is tautological and can never detect a mirror; and its doc premise is factually wrong (a camera looking toward +Z keeps seeing the world +X direction on its own right). In neatRacing the camera right axis is (-fZ, 0, fX), so a +Z-looking camera sees world +X on its LEFT.'
      required_change: 'Re-derive the expectation GEOMETRICALLY from the camera basis with no shared yaw algebra: f = normalize(cameraForward.xz), r = (-fZ, 0, fX), d = normalize(gazeTarget - robotPosition), along = d dot f, lateral = d dot r, phi = atan2(lateral, along), index = round(((PI - phi) mod 2PI) / 45deg) mod 8. Correct the misleading doc blocks and add a LATERAL contract: a spectator facing the car due south renders as left for a camera forward of [1,0,0] and as right for [-1,0,0], asserted on BOTH the runtime and the build-time path. The two RED-A assertions (front for a north heading, 2-step circular distance for a 90 deg heading change) must NOT be weakened or removed.'
  non_blocking_findings:
    - 'F3: artifacts/shared-validation.json is stale; the visible-window smoke and the artifact regeneration belong to 05-green-testing (P1-crowd-green).'
    - 'F4: the build-time gaze target is the camera position while the runtime gaze target is the car position. Accepted as a follow-on note (the build-time path approximates the chase rig); no change in this slice.'
    - 'F5: RESOLVED - the basis derivation cameraUp x cameraRight = cameraForward is the exact inverse of the browser-entry basis, so browser-entry.ts and frame-composer.ts MUST NOT be edited.'
    - 'F6: the frame-composer draw-state bag defaults imply a 180 deg-wrong forward before the first basis update; follow-on note for the 05-green-testing visible-window smoke.'
  fix_loop:
    - 'A NEW implementation-executor instance (not the previous one) applies F1 and F2.'
    - '04-implementing re-runs the targeted preflight (jest public.sprite.test.ts, tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit, eslint on the 3 slice files).'
    - '04-implementing re-dispatches a FRESH webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer and loops until APPROVE.'
  red_contract_note: 'The RED-A assertions are byte-preserved. The expectation HELPER body and two doc blocks are rewritten per F2 (de-tautologization plus a factually corrected premise) and one NEW lateral test is appended; no RED assertion is weakened, removed or relaxed.'
  handoff: 'fix-packet-P1-crowd-facing-relative-iteration-1 -> NEW implementation-executor -> preflight -> FRESH webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer'

    - 'AC-074 (role set) IMPLEMENTED: the runtime role union is widened to PublicRuntimeRole = seated | walker | standing | mechanic (public.sprite.ts:154) with the exported PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROLES roster (public.sprite.ts:205), and resolvePublicRuntimeRole stays the SINGLE resolver of the role.     - 'THE LONGITUDINAL TRACTION TERM: the tire model now also owns computeLongitudinalTractionLoss(slipAngle, speed, speedPercent) - the forward speed a sliding tire cannot hold - and the longitudinal integrator subtracts it from the tick-end speed (physics.step.service.ts step 4b, reading the tick-start slip like every other tick-start read in that integrator).'

## PlanUpdate - Step 14N drift-feel integration coupling design (02-researching, read-only)

- `date`: '2026-10-24'
- `step`: '14N'
- `agent`: '02-researching (Tier-1 drift-feel scout)'
- `slice_researched`: 'P1-drift-feel-red (the RED slice that owns the feel direction)'
- `research_artifact`: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md'
- `files_changed`: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (this tracker only) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (new). NO production file was touched.'
- `sub_orchestrators_used`: 'boundary-mapper (drift-yaw ownership chain, tick order, body-matrix composition) and implementation-pattern-scout (test/fixture contract inventory). Both read-only, both re-verified by the orchestrator against the source before anything was written down.'
- `pre_execute_hook`: 'neataptic-workflow-mcp-get_slice_context with slice_id P1-drift-feel-red was invoked as declared by the Step 14N packet.'

### The design model (the answer to the Step 14N research question)

> **The transient drift-yaw accumulator is a TRANSIENT GAIN modulation, and the drift-yaw offset stays exactly proportional to the slip angle:**
>
> ```
> driftYawOffset = slipAngle * (NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD + transientGain)
> ```
>
> The accumulator is a separate, bounded, dimensionless state advanced by a PURE step function in `examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts`, carried on `PhysicsCarState` (NOT on `DriftModelState`), stepped inside `physics.step.service.ts` after the drift model has produced `slipAngle` and before the offset is computed. It feeds the SINGLE existing `driftYawOffset` scalar, so `car.pass.ts` and `browser-entry.ts` are untouched.

Why this shape (the decisive reasons):

- **Zero straight-line yaw becomes EXACT by construction** - with `slipAngle === 0` the offset is `0` whatever the accumulator holds. An ADDITIVE yaw accumulator would carry a stale yaw onto the next straight line and would need a hard-reset contract. The additive alternative is documented in the research artifact and is NOT recommended (it also has a mid-range NULL where the body lands exactly on the travel direction and the proxy collapses to 0 for a frame or two, which resets the 3-consecutive-frame drift gate).
- **The AC-078 0.002 rad pin is provably invariant.** `tireYawFollowsBodyDuringDrift` measures `wheelYaw - bodyYaw` against `mount.rotationYawRad`, and the wheels are PARENTED onto the body matrix (`car.pass.ts:1598`), so the residual is independent of the offset magnitude. Enlarging the drift cannot move it.
- **`proportionalTractionLoss` is untouched.** The accumulator is VISUAL-ONLY: it never alters `x`, `y`, `heading`, `speed`, `slipAngle` or `lateralVelocity`, so the trajectory stays byte-identical and the 290 km/h ceiling (AC-079) cannot regress.
- **`car.pass.test.ts` stays green.** `DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_LIMIT_RAD` is DERIVED as `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD * NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD`, so it re-derives itself when the base gain moves, and the monotonicity sweep constrains the PASS, not the physics.

### DECISIVE finding 1 - the drift proxy is a V-SHAPED function of the visual gain, with a NULL at 1.0

The fixture measures the proxy from the RENDERED BODY MATRIX against the world-XZ travel chord (`docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html:789-822`), and the physics translates along `heading + slipAngle`. Therefore

```
proxy = |bodyYaw - travelDirection| = |slipAngle| * |GAIN_eff - 1|
```

The recorded baseline `0.049388550574608114 rad` is EXACTLY `0.5 x |slip|` with `|slip| = 0.098777101149216228 rad`, which confirms the identity to the last digit. Consequences the RED slice must internalise BEFORE pinning the floor:

- `GAIN_eff = 0.75` -> proxy 0.0247 (SLIDE SHRINKS); `GAIN_eff = 1.00` -> proxy **0.0000 - THE SLIDE VANISHES**; `GAIN_eff = 1.50` -> 0.0494 (equals today); `GAIN_eff = 2.00` -> 0.0988.
- A naive "raise the gain to feel more drift" move toward 1.0 makes the slide WEAKER while the offset magnitude looks BIGGER. The RED slice must record the `GAIN_eff = +1.0` NULL as a FORBIDDEN region, and is recommended to drive `GAIN_eff` DOWN (monotone, null-free) rather than up.
- The current `GAIN = 0.5` means the body yaw sits at only HALF the physical slip - the "mushy" read the user reported.

### DECISIVE finding 2 - AC-088's named lever CANNOT close the measured residual (plan-level correction required)

`analyzeWheelShading()` (fixture `:605-624`) reads the wheel VBO and averages `max(r,g,b)` of the VERTEX ALBEDO, split by local Y. The mesh builder states it outright (`car.pass.ts:555-556`): *"Vertex colors stay uniform rubber."* - the OBS-20 tire gradient is a FRAGMENT-stage effect (`car.pass.ts:320-329`, uniforms `uTireGradientRadius` / `uTireGradientBrightFactor` / `uTireGradientDarkFactor`) that this measurement path NEVER observes. The mesh is top/bottom symmetric, so `upperAvg === lowerAvg === 0.28565` and the measured gradient is identically zero - and INVARIANT to all three named AC-088 levers.

⇒ **A RED contract of the form "the current fixture's measured gradient is strictly non-zero" is UNSATISFIABLE by tuning the named constants and would strand the tune slice.** The AC-088 lever must be re-scoped to the MEASUREMENT (sample the shaded framebuffer) or the contract must move to its existing jest owner, `examples/neatRacing/engine/lighting.test.ts` (`describe('fixed-space tire lighting (OBS-20)')`). The Step 14N RED packet currently names `examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/car.pass.test.ts` as the tire-gradient file - that is the WRONG owner and the RED slice must correct the file list.

### RED contracts the slice must author (recommended)

1. The AC-087 floor `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD`, pinned against the measured baseline `0.049388550574608114 rad`, with the recorded feel DIRECTION (bigger slide vs crisper recovery) and the chosen named lever, plus the forbidden `GAIN_eff = +1.0` null.
2. **ZERO STRAIGHT-LINE BODY YAW - a NEW contract.** No assertion anywhere in the repo covers it today (`physics.step.service.test.ts:247-252` pins `speed === MAX` and `slipAngle === 0` but asserts NOTHING about yaw). Under the recommended model it is exact by construction; the contract must exist to keep it that way.
3. A drift-exit reset / recovery contract bound to the recorded decay constant.
4. A regression guard that the 3-consecutive-frame drift gate is never reset by the transient (a single frame below `DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_RAD = 0.01` resets `driftProxyRunFrames` and can break AC-078 AND AC-079 together).
5. The AC-088 measurement/owner correction above.

### Constants that move

- `NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD` (`drift.model.ts:97`, today `0.5`) - the base gain / magnitude lever, with the V-shaped proxy relation and the `+1.0` null.
- NEW in `drift.model.ts`: `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_MAX` (must be chosen so `|GAIN_eff| * |slipAngle| < PI/2`, the `physics.step.service.test.ts:162` pin), `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_RATE_PER_S` (build) and `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_DECAY_PER_S` (recovery - THESE TWO TRADE OFF, and that trade-off IS the feel decision), and `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD` (the AC-087 floor; the browser fixture hardcodes its own constants, so the floor needs a single source of truth AND a mirrored literal).
- CANDIDATE in `car.pass.ts`: `NEATRACING_TIRE_GRADIENT_RADIUS_M`, decoupling `uTireGradientRadius` from `NEATRACING_WHEEL_HUB_HEIGHT_M` (today `car.pass.ts:1469` feeds the wheel-MOUNT constant into the lighting uniform) - correct hygiene, but per DECISIVE finding 2 it CANNOT by itself close the measured residual.
- MUST NOT MOVE (physics constants - they change the trajectory and would break AC-079/AC-089): `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_MPS`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LONGITUDINAL_TRACTION_LOSS_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD`.

### State ownership and tick order (recorded)

- `PhysicsCarState` (`physics.step.service.ts:73-112`) owns the new numeric field; the session (`host/race-session.ts:81-89`) replaces the record wholesale each tick, so the field must be carried forward. There is NO worker / postMessage boundary today (main thread only), so no clone/transfer concerns.
- `DriftModelState` has exactly TWO fields and is byte-identity pinned by AC-047D (`drift.model.test.ts:309-327`), so the accumulator is a SEPARATE type in `drift.model.ts` and is NOT a `DriftModelState` field.
- Tick order: rAF -> `handleFrame` -> 0..4 fixed ticks of 1/60 s -> per tick `stepPhysics` then `stepRaceRules` -> `hud.update` -> `composer.drawFrame` -> `browser-entry.ts:941` -> `carPass.draw`. The accumulator is stepped in TICK order (after the drift model produced `slipAngle`, before the offset is computed); the body matrix is built ONCE per rendered frame from the last tick's offset, exactly as today.
- The determinism test compares run A vs run B of the SAME code (never a golden literal), so adding a field to `PhysicsCarState` is safe.

### Blockers / open items owned by the RED slice

- The feel DIRECTION (bigger slide vs crisper recovery) and the floor VALUE are NOT invented here - they are the RED slice's explicit decision per the Step 14N amendment note.
- The slip envelope at the pinned `physics.step.service.test.ts` fixture is not yet measured, so `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_MAX` cannot be bounded yet.
- AC-088 needs a plan-level lever correction (measurement) and a file-owner correction (`engine/lighting.test.ts`, not `car.pass.test.ts`).

### Carried-forward residuals (recorded, not owned by Step 14N)

### DECISIVE FINDINGS (arcade-refs)

- **The user verdict is CORRECT, and stronger than stated: the current drift model is not merely "slow" - the countersteer CANNOT catch the slide, it MIRRORS it.** Reproduced the model's equations and simulated them at 60 Hz:
  - **25 m/s (the fixture's 90 km/h operating point), full left steer:** the slip plateaus at **-4.50 deg** (proxy 0.0392 rad) - too small to read, and it takes ~0.25 s / ~0.75 s to reach 63 % / 95 % of that. **This is the "tilt too slow / icy" complaint.**
  - **89 m/s, full left steer:** the slip reaches **-65.8 deg AND KEEPS GROWING**; the effective damping collapses **4.0/s -> 0.51/s** as the slip grows (more slip => less traction => less damping => more slip). **Positive feedback, not a grip budget.**
  - **Full COUNTERSTEER:** 25 m/s -> the slip crosses zero and **parks at +4.48 deg**, a mirror-image equilibrium of the same size; 89 m/s -> **-65.8 deg becomes +52.2 deg** and never recovers. **The countersteer inverts the car.**
  - **Root cause (verified in source, two independent parts):** (1) the "centrifugal" outward push is a function of the YAW RATE, and the yaw rate is a function of the STEER - so countersteering REVERSES the push and the two terms ADD instead of opposing; (2) the countersteer gate `steer * sign(slip) > 0` **closes the instant the slip crosses zero**, switching off the very authority that could catch the slide. Plus the countersteer magnitude is tiny: 12/s x speedPercent = 3.4 m/s^2 at 25 m/s vs the push's 8.4 m/s^2.
  - **=> "Bounce-back must be sharper" is a MISSING-AUTHORITY / WRONG-GATE problem, not a rate problem. Raising `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S` (the code-map scout's lever #5) would make the inversion FASTER and HARDER, not better.**
- **C1 (verified):** the production `NEATRACING_PHYSICS_CENTRIFUGAL_MULTIPLIER` is **1.5** (`physics.step.service.ts:184`), NOT the 0.3 that `drift.model.ts:119` claims in its JSDoc. The JSDoc is wrong and every feel number derived from it is wrong.
- **C6:** `outwardPush` is dimensionally inconsistent - `yawRatePerTick` is radians PER TICK, so `rad/tick x m/s` is not m/s. The correct centripetal term is `yawRate[rad/s] x speed[m/s] x dt`.
- **C7:** `0.6 x |slip| x speed x speedPercent` = **24.2 m/s^2** at 26 deg / 89 m/s, i.e. **larger than the engine's 17.8 m/s^2**. The car cannot hold speed in a deep slide.
- **Proxy identity (confirmed to the last digit, and independently by both repo scouts):** `proxy = |slip| x |GAIN - 1|`, so the recorded **0.049388550574608114 rad** baseline implies `|slip| ~ 0.0988 rad = 5.66 deg`. **The proxy is V-shaped in the gain with a NULL at GAIN = 1.0** - raising the gain makes the slide WEAKER. The only monotone direction is DOWN.

### THE MODEL (stated explicitly, as the charter requires)

- Seven stages, all in `drift.model.ts`: (0) drift latch - `turnSign` latched at entry; (1) committed drift angle - rate-limited ramp IN (`ENTRY_RATE_RAD_PER_S`), linear unwind OUT (`EXIT_RATE_RAD_PER_S`), clamped to `+-MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD`; (2) tire saturation as a BUDGET `gripFactor = 1/(1 + RATE x max(0,|slip| - THRESHOLD))`; (3) physical chase `vLat += (tan(committed) x speed - vLat) x (1 - exp(-dt x gripFactor / TAU))`; (4) **countersteer authority applied AGAINST the slide** `vLat += turnSign x COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS x |steer| x speedPercent x dt`; (5) hard zero `if (!drifting && |slip| < SNAP_BACK_ZERO) { vLat = 0; committed = 0; }`; (6) saturating speed scrub; (7) **visible pose as a SECOND-ORDER spring-damper** `poseTarget = slip x GAIN + POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD x steer x speedPercent x min(1, |slip|/FULL_SLIP_RAD)`.
- **Sign convention pinned to production (verified):** `lateralVelocity > 0` = the velocity lies LEFT of the heading, so a LEFT turn produces a NEGATIVE slip and the visible offset `slip x GAIN` is negative. **The upstream research draft's `-committed` in the pose target is a SIGN ERROR under this convention and would mirror the whole drift - the implementer must use the corrected form in the research artifact D1.**

### THE CONSTANT SET (for `drift.model.ts`)

- `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD = 0.45` (25.8 deg; was `Math.PI/2` - and note it is UNUSED inside its own module, so it is an envelope pin, not a lever) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_MPS = 15` (unchanged) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_ENTRY_RATE_RAD_PER_S = 3.5` (201 deg/s) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_EXIT_RATE_RAD_PER_S = 2.0` (115 deg/s) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S = 0.045` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD = 0.20` (was 0.25) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD = 2` (unchanged) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS = 70` (m/s^2) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_MIN_SLIP_RAD = 0.02` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SNAP_BACK_ZERO_SLIP_RAD = 0.02` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 = 324` (omega = 18 rad/s, f = 2.86 Hz) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S = 12.6` (zeta = 0.35 => 31 % first overshoot) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD = 0.08` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_FULL_SLIP_RAD = 0.10` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SPEED_SCRUB_COEFF_PER_S = 0.25` (was 0.6) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD = 0.5` (UNCHANGED - it stays the base gain).
- **Retired by this model:** `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S` (4) -> `SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S` + the saturation budget; `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S` (12) -> `COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS`; `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LONGITUDINAL_TRACTION_LOSS_RATE_PER_S` (0.6) -> `SPEED_SCRUB_COEFF_PER_S` (0.25, saturating rather than proportional-to-speed).

### MEASURED PREDICTIONS (my own 60 Hz simulation of the new model; full steer at t=1.0 s, full countersteer at t=3.0 s)

| Metric | Current model | New model |
|---|---|---|
| Entry: 63 % / 95 % of the hold slide | ~0.25 s / ~0.75 s @25 m/s | **0.10 s / 0.20 s** @both speeds |
| Hold slide @89 m/s | -65.8 deg and growing | **-25.94 deg, BOUNDED** |
| Hold slide @25 m/s | -4.50 deg (invisible) | **-25.83 deg** |
| Visual proxy at hold | 0.0392 rad @25 m/s | **0.2266 rad = 4.6x the 0.0494 baseline** |
| Countersteer: slip at +0.1 / +0.2 / +0.3 s | -54.4 / +10.6 / +28.1 deg (MIRRORED) | **-18.96 / -7.01 / 0.00 deg** |
| Visible swing-past | **0.00 deg** (structurally impossible - a first-order lateral model cannot overshoot) | **-14.02 deg at +0.1 s = 4.83 deg past the hold pose**, then a decaying ring (+2.61 -> -0.51 -> -0.53 -> +0.23 -> 0) |
| Residual body yaw on a straight line | 0 (exact) | **-0.07 deg ~ 0** (the slip-gated steer-yaw term preserves the zero-straight-line guarantee) |
| Speed scrub @89 m/s | 24.2 m/s^2 (> engine 17.8) | **10.0 m/s^2** (the engine still wins) |

### MERGE RECOMMENDATION (criterion: fun / exciting)

- **The already-recorded coupling design's "Track A" (visual-only transient gain) is a strict SUBSET of this model.** The coupling design's transient gain and this model's pose spring-damper are the SAME mechanism (a second-order visual channel); this model just sources it from the physical slip instead of a synthetic gain, so the visual swing and the physical catch become one coherent thing.
- **Track A alone CANNOT satisfy the user verdict.** The operative clause is *"bounce-back must be sharper"* and the bounce-back is PHYSICAL. A cosmetic swing on a car that is still sliding the wrong way is not a fix. If the budget cannot absorb the re-baselining, Track A is a reasonable INTERIM (drive the gain DOWN: proxy `0.0988 x 1.5 = 0.148 rad` = 3.0x baseline, byte-identical trajectory) but it must be recorded as **cosmetic-only**.
- **RECOMMENDED MIX: (1) the physical model as a NEW slice with re-baselining; (2) the pose spring-damper as the visual half of it; (3) the AC-087 floor re-pinned on the DETERMINISTIC unit proxy, not the noisy browser proxy (recorded spread 0.0494 / 0.0603 / 0.3599 rad - a floor pinned to 0.0494 would sit inside the noise band).**
